reason: This passage concerns the plagues of Egypt (frogs, boils, hail, locusts, darkness) and focuses on Moses confronting Pharaoh and executing God's commands. The narrative perspective is not that of a leader dealing with ungrateful people, but rather a third-person account of God's instructions to Moses and the resulting demonstrations of divine power against Egypt. The antagonist is Pharaoh (whose heart is repeatedly hardened), not the Israelite people. No mention is made of the Israelites being ungrateful in this fragment. The perspective is primarily divine (God commanding), not that of a leader frustrated with his own people.
